parts.stem:
The electrochemical cell in (d) was set up again but this time the concentration of $\text{Co}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ was $0.050\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

The Nernst equation can be used to calculate the value of an electrode potential at different concentrations.

$$E = E^\circ + (0.059/z)\log[\text{Co}^{2+}\text{(aq)}]$$ Nernst equation

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Iron(III) ions can oxidise vanadium metal.

Construct an equation for the reaction of an excess of iron(III) ions with vanadium metal. Use of the Data Booklet will be helpful.
